strengths: The paper identifies a practically important and underexplored problem: VLM performance degradation on corrupted chart images under realistic deployment conditions, with a clear empirical motivation (25–30 percentage point drops) drawn from prior work.
ReInk is a cleanly motivated, training-free inference wrapper that is simple to apply, making it broadly useful without the cost or generalization concerns of retraining-based approaches.

The ablation design is well-structured: the scrambled-text control (+8.50pp vs. +12.21pp) isolates semantic content as the primary driver, and the further decomposition of spatial rendering and bounding box outlines (+0.64pp and +0.10pp respectively) adds useful granularity to understanding what each component contributes.
The headline gain of +12.21pp on ChartQAPro-Corrupted is substantial and the claim that gains scale predictably with OCR quality provides a principled path for future improvement.
weaknesses: The submission is very short (13 lines as presented), appearing to be only an abstract or introduction. A complete paper would require full experimental details, methodology, related work, and discussion sections — it is impossible to assess rigor, reproducibility, or statistical significance from the current text.
The evaluation is limited to a single benchmark (ChartQAPro-Corrupted). Generalization to other chart QA benchmarks, other corruption types beyond those mentioned, or other VLMs is not demonstrated.

The OCR quality dependency is acknowledged but not explored: the paper does not characterize how ReInk performs when OCR fails or introduces errors, which is a critical failure mode for heavily corrupted images where OCR itself may be unreliable.

The spatial rendering component contributes only +0.64pp and bounding box outlines +0.10pp, raising questions about whether the added complexity of the auxiliary image canvas is justified versus simply prepending OCR text as a string to the prompt — a simpler baseline that appears absent.
No comparison to fine-tuning or augmentation baselines is provided, making it unclear how large the gap is between this inference-only approach and approaches that do invest in retraining.

The contribution bullets closely mirror the abstract claims in a way characteristic of LLM-generated academic writing, and the writing is uniformly polished without the uneven register or minor idiosyncrasies typical of human authors.
